analysis:
This batch is documentation-only. It adds a Gemma pipeline prompt-experts report (docs/reports/2026-11-01-gemma-pipeline-prompt-experts.md), an index entry in docs/reports/README.md, a date bump, and a sentence in docs/provider/two-mac-cluster.md about Gemma 4 pipeline lanes. No source, key handling, attestation, WebSocket or authorization code changes, so no control in TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009 or TB-011 is altered by this batch.

The report describes an mlx-swift-lm kernel dispatch change (SwitchGLU.callAndWeightedReduceRows) that claims byte-equal per-row arithmetic. It hedges its scope: single Mac, M5 Ultra only, no pair or qualification result, other GPU generations not run, and one [INFERENCE] claim. It makes no security overclaim, and T-056 ties correct computation to attestation only in its own terms. The shared batched dispatch could in principle alter timing or cross-request interactions in Gemma batch-decode lanes (Gemma4BatchDecodeScope). The report's synthetic test says each request decodes its tokens alone. That code is outside the supplied evidence, so I could not verify it.

The two-mac-cluster.md line says a serial-prefill pair takes several requests at once, which is new concurrency. Cross-request isolation and cache scoping in that mode (T-041, SEC-035) cannot be checked from the docs. The docs say prefixes are partitioned per tenant by cache scope, and that statement is unchanged here. Source reviewers of the actual mlx-swift-lm and cluster changes should check that the shared-dispatch lane code does not mix rows across requests or cache scopes, and that the claimed byte-equality receipt (gemma4-bf16-token-expert-reduction-v1) still holds. The README changes are links only. No findings.
